profile.statistic: the bounding-box overlap ratio a_o = area(Bp n Bgt) / area(Bp u Bgt) — intersection over union, IoU — which decides whether a detection counts as correct. Unlike the other three thresholds this instrument has read, it is not a statistic computed on data but a stipulation of an evaluation protocol; and this literature writes the same threshold in two units, 0.5 and 50%, which is why the profile carries focus_equivalents (instrument 0.4).
profile.deriving_document: Everingham, M., Van Gool, L., Williams, C. K. I., Winn, J. & Zisserman, A. (2010), 'The PASCAL Visual Object Classes (VOC) Challenge', International Journal of Computer Vision 88(2), 303-338, doi:10.1007/s11263-009-0275-7, section 4.2 'Bounding box evaluation'. Read at source 2026-08-08 (https://homepages.inf.ed.ac.uk/ckiw/postscript/ijcv_voc09.pdf, sha256 bda24d6d51d58815b6816cb483394356f692d897002c280014fa4fd4bbdc72cd, pdftotext 24.02.0 -layout, quotations checked against the PDF): 'To be considered a correct detection, the area of overlap ao between the predicted bounding box Bp and ground truth bounding box Bgt must exceed 0.5 (50%) by the formula [...]' followed immediately by the reason: 'The threshold of 50% was set deliberately low to account for inaccuracies in bounding boxes in the ground truth data, for example defining the bounding box for a highly non-convex object, e.g. a person with arms and legs spread, is somewhat subjective.'
